Question: Does the Space Force have soldiers in space?
Old_Answer: No, nor has it any plans for them any time soon. The Space Force was created after 40 years of bipartisan recommendations to preserve and protect the satellites that are now critical not only the the military but to the economies of America and its allies. It did not steal its uniform from Battlestar Galactica or its seal from Star Trek. It was not Donald Trump’s idea, and his administration and Congress only really got behind it after China and India demonstrated advanced anti-satellite capability and a Russian orbital device approached a $3 billion intelligence satellite so close, it had to take evasive action. Only then, belatedly, was the Space Force formed from about 12,000 uniformed service personnel and contractors already working on space defense but scattered across various other branches, and organized into a whole under the already existing joint DOD Space Command that has existed in one form or another since the 1980s. So no, the Space Force isn’t a pointless space navy and has no personnel in space (except occasionally the two NASA astronauts inherited from the Air Force), but as an instructor in the Air Command and Staff College told me in 2018, wherever people go, the police and the military will eventually have to follow. So stay tuned. The true story and the history of the Space Force is fascinating and surprising, and is chronicled along with two dozen science fiction stories illustrating its current and future mission in my new anthology, Tales of the United States Space Force, available now from Baen Books and in bookstores everywhere.
